==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|instrument}}, from {{der|en|fro|instrument}}, from {{der|en|la|īnstrūmentum||an implement, tool}},
From {{suffix|la|īnstruō|t1=build, construct; arrange|mentum||nocat=1}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɪnstɹəmənt/|/ˈɪnstɹʊmənt/}}
** {{audio|en|En-us-instrument.ogg|a=California,US}}
* {{hyph|en|in|stru|ment}}

===Noun===
{{wikidata lexeme|L4613}}
{{en-noun}}

# A [[device]] used to produce [[music]].
#: {{ux|en|The violinist was a master of her '''instrument'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=William Cornishe [''i.e.'', {{w|William Cornysh}}]| chapter=In the Fleete Made by Me William Cornishe otherwise Called Nyshwhete Chapelman with the Most Famose and Noble Kyng [[w:Henry VII of England|Henry the VII.]] His Reygne the XIX. Yere the Moneth of July. A Treatise betwene Trouth, and Information.|mainauthor=w:John Skelton|editor=[[w:John Stow|J[ohn] S[tow]]]| title=Pithy Pleasaunt and Profitable Workes of Maister Skelton, Poete Laureate| location=Imprinted at London: In [[w:Fleet Street|Fletestreate]], neare vnto [[w:St Dunstan-in-the-West|St Dunstan-in-the-West]] by Thomas Marshe| year=1568| oclc=54747393| title2=Pithy Pleasaunt and Profitable Workes of Maister Skelton, Poete Laureate to King Henry the VIIIth|location2=London|publisher2=Printed for C. Davis in [[w:Paternoster Row|Pater-noster Row]]| year2=1736| page2=290| pageurl2=https://books.google.com/books?id=Ry8JAAAAQAAJ&pg=PA290| oclc2=731569711| passage=''The Harpe.'' {{...}} A harper with his [[wrest#Noun|wreſt]] maye tune the harpe wrong / Mys tunying of an '''Inſtrument''' ſhal hurt a true ſonge}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=1997-08-09|author=Edward Rothstein|title=A Comeback for the Viola. No Joking.|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1997/08/09/arts/a-comeback-for-the-viola-no-joking.html
|passage=But those who attack violists shouldn't throw resin. Once the ergonomic viola catches on what '''instrument''' will be immune?|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210227054018/https://www.nytimes.com/1997/08/09/arts/a-comeback-for-the-viola-no-joking.html}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=2008-05-30|author=The New York Times|title=Pop and Rock Listings|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2008/05/30/arts/music/30pop.html
|passage=MOHAMMAD REZA SHAJARIAN (Thursday) Renowned in his native Iran, the vocalist Mohammad Reza Shajarian has been performing since the 1960s, and is now widely considered one of the finest classical Persian singers in the world. Mr. Shajarian’s son, Homayoun Shajarian, will provide additional vocals and tombak (goblet drum), while Ensemble Ava, a four-piece, will contribute additional instrumentation on the ancient Persian '''instruments''' barbat (short-necked lute), tar (long-necked lute), kamancheh (spike fiddle) and daf (frame drum).|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220409091442/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/05/30/arts/music/30pop.html}}
# A [[means]] or [[agency]] for achieving an aspect.
#* {{RQ:Orczy Miss Elliott|chapter=The Tremarn Case|passage=“There the cause of death was soon ascertained ; the victim of this daring outrage had been stabbed to death from ear to ear with a long, sharp '''instrument''', in shape like an antique stiletto, which {{...}} was subsequently found under the cushions of the hansom. {{...}}”}}
#* {{RQ:Time
|date=January 11, 1963
|title=The World
|url=https://archive.org/details/time-1963-11-22/Time%201963-01-11/
|volume=LXXXI
|issue=2
|page=32
|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/time-1963-11-22/Time%201963-01-11/page/32/
|column=3
|text=On the rocky island of Tungyin, 50 miles off the coast of Red China, is the headquarters of a little-known military unit called the Anti-Communist Salvation Army. The secret army, 30,000 strong, is Chiang Kai-shek's '''instrument''' for the long-promised return to the mainland.}}
# A [[measuring]] or [[display]]ing device.
#: {{ux|en|The '''instrument''' detected an increase in radioactivity.}}
# A [[tool]], [[implement]] used for [[manipulation]] or [[measurement]].
#: {{ux|en|The dentist set down his tray of '''instruments'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|The scientist recorded the temperature with a thermometer, but wished he had a more accurate '''instrument'''.}}
## {{lb|en|aviation|usually|in the plural}} {{ellipsis of|en|flight instrument}}.
##: {{ux|en|Flight within clouds must be made by reference to your '''instruments'''.}}
# {{senseid|en|legal document}} {{lb|en|legal}} A legal document, such as a [[contract]], [[deed]], [[trust]], [[mortgage]], [[power]], [[indenture]], or [[will]], or any of a class of [[negotiable]] ones (which can be exchanged for value or money).
#: {{hypo|en|negotiable instrument|;|cheque<id:Q80042>|check<id:Q80042>|note<id:document promising payment>|draft<id:order for payment>|promissory note}}
#: {{ux|en|A bond indenture is the '''instrument''' that gives a bond its value.}}
#: {{ux|en|Negotiable '''instruments''' are the foundation of the debt markets.}}
# {{lb|en|figuratively}} A person used as a mere tool for achieving a goal.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare King John|V|ii|passage=Or useful serving man and '''instrument''', / To any sovereign state.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1670|author=w:John Dryden|title=w:The Conquest of Granada
|passage=The bold are but the '''instruments''' o' the wise.}}

#: {{ux|en|an '''instrumented''' test article}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To devise, conceive, [[cook up]], plan.
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=15 Apr 78|journal=Gay Community News|page=10|author=Mitzel|title=An Evening and an Afternoon with James Purdy|text=When the Lit.
